html: Tama Dujo is an Indigenous community of the upper Magdalena valley in Huila, southern Colombia. Its name recalls the Tama, a people recorded by Spanish writers in the 1500s and 1600s in the forests between the upper Magdalena and the Caquetá; their language, thought to be Tukanoan, is lost. Little is written about the community. Like many groups in Colombia, it holds land as a reserve, or resguardo, and its people also share heritage with the Nasa, or Páez, of the nearby highlands, and with the Pijao.
